title: Indonesia | OJK Good Governance, Risk Management Certification and Whistleblowing
tagline: Run the boards, keep risk certificates valid, fund staff development and protect whistleblowers the way OJK expects.
description:
A compliance quest for conventional commercial banks in Indonesia, built on rules issued by the Financial Services Authority, **Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK)**:

- **POJK 17/2023** on governance of commercial banks (Penerapan Tata Kelola bagi Bank Umum) and its implementing circular **SEOJK 14/2025**: principles, boards, committees, conflicts of interest, governance reports and self-assessment.
- **SEOJK 28/2022** on risk management certification (Sertifikasi Manajemen Risiko) and **POJK 24/2022** on developing bank human resources: who must be certified, three-year validity, yearly refreshers, the six-month replacement rule and the 3.5 percent development spending floor.
- **POJK 12/2024** on anti-fraud strategy (Strategi Anti Fraud): whistleblowing, reporter protection and investigation.

It is for directors, commissioners, committee members, executive officers and officers who must hold risk management certificates, and for governance, HR, compliance and anti-fraud teams. OJK requires these people to hold valid certificates and refresh them at least yearly, and expects boards to know the governance rules they apply. Fit and proper assessment is covered in general terms. The quest builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own policies or the current text of OJK's rules.
audience: Directors, commissioners and members of board committees of Indonesian commercial banks
Executive officers and officers in risk, compliance, audit, credit, treasury, IT and finance who need risk management certificates
Corporate secretaries, governance and compliance teams preparing governance reports and self-assessments
HR and learning teams managing certification registers and the staff development budget
Anti-fraud units and managers who receive or handle whistleblowing reports
outcomes: Apply POJK 17/2023's principles and sixteen aspects, and meet its governance report and self-assessment deadlines
Check board and committee composition, independence and conduct against OJK's rules
Explain fit and proper assessment in general terms and the nomination committee's role
Keep risk management certificates valid under SEOJK 28/2022 and act on lapses within OJK's timeframe
Plan and evidence staff development spending of at least 3.5 percent of prior-year gross salary cost
Run a confidential whistleblowing channel within the POJK 12/2024 anti-fraud strategy and prevent retaliation

sessions.title: Good Governance under POJK 17/2023: Principles, Boards and Reports
sessions.summary: Meet OJK's umbrella governance rule for commercial banks: the five principles, the sixteen aspects, Indonesia's two-tier boards, the twice-yearly self-assessment, the annual governance report and the sanctions ladder.
objectives: Explain the purpose, scope and status of POJK 17/2023 for conventional commercial banks
Apply the five governance principles to everyday bank decisions
Describe the roles of the GMS, the Board of Directors and the Board of Commissioners
Plan the governance self-assessment and governance report within OJK's deadlines
Recognise the administrative sanctions and fines OJK can impose for governance breaches

cards.title: Day one in the Corporate Secretary's office
cards.setting: Corporate Secretary's office, Bank Rinjani Raya head office, Jakarta. Monday, 8:15 am.

lines.text: You have just joined Bank Rinjani Raya, a fictional conventional commercial bank with branches from Medan to Makassar, as a governance and compliance analyst.
Welcome! I'm Lestari Handayani, corporate secretary. This office keeps the governance machinery running: board meetings, minutes, the annual governance report and our self-assessment for OJK.
Hendra Gunawan, director in charge of compliance. Good timing. The self-assessment is due and I have a list of loose ends.
Putu Ayu Saraswati, head of HR. One loose end is mine: two directors' risk management certificates run out this year, and our training spend looks thin.
Yosef Manurung, independent commissioner and chair of the risk monitoring committee. I would also like to know why nobody has reviewed our committee charters since 2021.
Sorry to join the call late. Fajar Ramadhan, credit officer in Makassar. I need to report something about a loan file, but I don't know who to tell, or whether I'll get into trouble.
Five stages, one mission: get Bank Rinjani Raya ready for OJK's review. Stage one is the Governance Compass. Learn the map before we fix anything.

scenes.heading: One supervisor for banks
scenes.narration: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority, Otoritas Jasa Keuangan or OJK, licenses and supervises commercial banks. It issues binding regulations, called POJK, and implementing circulars, called SEOJK.

scenes.heading: POJK 17 of 2023
scenes.narration: On 14 September 2023 OJK issued POJK 17 of 2023 on governance for commercial banks. It took effect the day it was promulgated and revoked the 2016 governance regulation, POJK 55 of 2016.

scenes.heading: Five principles
scenes.narration: Every bank must apply good governance in all its business, at every level of the organisation, built on five principles: transparency, accountability, responsibility, independence and fairness.

scenes.heading: Sixteen aspects
scenes.narration: The regulation lists sixteen areas where governance must show: the boards and committees, conflicts of interest, compliance, audit, risk management, remuneration, related-party lending, reporting, strategy, shareholders, anti-fraud, sustainable finance and group governance.

scenes.heading: OJK assesses
scenes.narration: OJK assesses how well each bank applies governance. Since June 2025, circular SEOJK 14 of 2025 sets out how banks score themselves on all sixteen factors.

cards.title: Indonesia's two-tier bank structure
cards.caption: Based on Articles 1, 6, 20, 22, 35, 38 and 49 of POJK 17/2023. The shareholders' meeting sits at the top; supervision and management are split between two separate boards.

items.label: General Meeting of Shareholders (RUPS)
items.detail: Holds the powers the law and articles do not give the boards; appoints board members after the nomination committee's advice.

items.label: Board of Commissioners (Dewan Komisaris)
items.detail: Supervises how the directors manage the bank and advises them; at least half its members are independent.

items.label: Board of Directors (Direksi)
items.detail: Manages the bank and is fully responsible for that management; at least three members.

items.label: Control units
items.detail: Internal audit, risk management and compliance units, which the directors must set up.

items.label: Executive officers and staff
items.detail: Run the business within the policies, limits and controls set above them.

cards.question: Which set lists the five good governance principles that POJK 17/2023 requires banks to apply?
options: Prudence, profitability, transparency, loyalty and fairness
Transparency, accountability, responsibility, independence and fairness
Accountability, growth, independence, secrecy and responsibility
Integrity, efficiency, transparency, seniority and fairness
cards.explanation: Article 2 names transparency (keterbukaan), accountability (akuntabilitas), responsibility (tanggung jawab), independence (independensi) and fairness (kewajaran). Prudence and integrity matter too, but they appear elsewhere in the rules, not in this list.

cards.title: The two boards in plain words
cards.body:
Indonesian commercial banks have **two boards**, not one:

- The **Board of Directors (Direksi)** manages the bank and is fully responsible for that management. It must act in good faith and prudently, apply governance, risk management and compliance in an integrated way, and answer to shareholders through the GMS.
- The **Board of Commissioners (Dewan Komisaris)** supervises the directors' policies and management, advises them and answers for that oversight. It directs, monitors and evaluates governance, risk management and compliance.
- Commissioners **may not take part in operational decisions**, except narrow cases such as funding to related parties under OJK's lending-limit rules, or what the articles or the law require. Even then the directors stay responsible for management.
- Each board needs a **binding charter** (pedoman dan tata tertib kerja) covering duties, decision procedures, ethics, meetings, prohibitions, performance evaluation and how the two boards work together.

cards.title: Principle or practice?
cards.prompt: Match each governance principle with an everyday practice that shows it.

pairs.right: Publishing the annual governance report on the bank's website
Each director has defined duties and is evaluated against them
The bank follows laws and regulations in everything it does
Board members decide free of pressure from the controlling shareholder
Minority shareholders and other stakeholders are treated equitably

cards.title: Real case: OJK announces POJK 17/2023 (2023)
cards.body:
On **19 September 2023** OJK announced its new governance regulation for commercial banks in press release SP 124/GKPB/OJK/IX/2023.

- OJK's chief executive for banking supervision, Dian Ediana Rae, called governance fundamental for banks to grow soundly, and stressed values, ethics and integrity.
- He sent a pointed message to **controlling shareholders**: do not issue policies, take decisions or act towards the bank in ways that breach OJK rules or the law, or run the bank unsoundly.
- OJK said the rules were updated for the digital banking ecosystem and its new risks, follow the 2023 P2SK Law on financial sector development, and draw on international standards from the Basel Committee, the OECD and the IFC.
- He asked everyone involved in a bank to understand their own position, role and responsibility.

**Lesson:** governance is not just a board matter. The regulation also sets clearer limits on how owners may behave towards the bank they control.

cards.title: The self-assessment calendar
cards.setting: Board meeting room, 14th floor, Jakarta. Tuesday, 10:00 am.

lines.text: At my last bank the governance self-assessment was a once-a-year exercise. Is that still fine?
Not any more. POJK 17/2023 requires a self-assessment at least twice a year, in step with the bank soundness rating periods, and the results form part of the governance report.
And the governance report itself?
Prepared at each financial year-end, sent to OJK and to our controlling shareholder, and published on our website, all within four months after the year ends.
What happens if we miss that?
First we are 'late'. If we still haven't filed one month after the deadline, OJK treats the report as not submitted at all. And the sanctions ladder starts.
Which brings me to this year's draft. Two factors came out weak. Our director of operations has an idea about that...

cards.title: The draft governance report
cards.situation: It is late April. The governance report is almost ready. The self-assessment rates two factors as weak: committee charters are out of date, and the conflict of interest register is incomplete. The director of operations suggests improving the picture before anything goes to OJK or onto the website. What do you recommend to Lestari?

choices.text: Submit and publish on time with honest ratings, plus an action plan that names owners and dates.
choices.outcome: Right. The report is due to OJK, the controlling shareholder and the website within four months of year-end, and the self-assessment is an integral part of it. OJK evaluates self-assessment results and can ask for an action plan with deadlines anyway, so a candid rating with a credible plan builds trust.

choices.text: Upgrade both factors to 'satisfactory' because the fixes are already planned.
choices.outcome: Poor. OJK evaluates the self-assessment and can order a special examination of the bank's governance improvements. Inflated ratings undermine the transparency principle and can turn a weakness into an integrity problem for the people who signed off.

choices.text: Hold the report for a few weeks until the charters are updated, then file.
choices.outcome: Poor. Filing after the deadline makes the bank late, and after one more month OJK treats it as not filed. Missing the date also breaches the reporting duty in its own right.

choices.text: File on time, but describe the two weak areas in vague general wording.
choices.outcome: Partly right: the deadline is met. But vague wording weakens transparency and OJK reviews the self-assessment against what its supervisors see. Say clearly what is weak and how you will fix it.

cards.title: From the 2016 rule to sixteen-factor scoring
cards.caption: Dates from POJK 17/2023, OJK press release SP 124/GKPB/OJK/IX/2023 and OJK's FAQ on SEOJK 14/SEOJK.03/2025.

items.label: POJK 55/2016
items.detail: OJK's earlier governance regulation for commercial banks.

items.label: POJK 17/2023 issued
items.detail: Promulgated and in force the same day; POJK 55/2016 revoked.

items.label: OJK explains the new rule
items.detail: Press release stresses integrity and limits on controlling shareholders.

items.label: SEOJK 14/2025 in force
items.detail: Implementing circular: 16 assessment factors and a self-assessment worksheet.

items.label: First 16-factor self-assessment
items.detail: Banks report a self-assessment covering all 16 factors for the first time.

cards.title: One of the sixteen aspects?
cards.prompt: POJK 17/2023 lists sixteen areas where good governance must show. Sort each item.

items.text: Handling conflicts of interest
Anti-fraud strategy, including anti-bribery
Sustainable finance, including social and environmental responsibility
Funding to related parties and large exposures
Integrity of reporting and IT systems
Governance within the bank's business group
Maximising the share price every quarter
Choosing branch opening hours
Approving the annual marketing budget

cards.question: Bank Rinjani Raya's financial year ends on 31 December. By when must its governance report reach OJK and appear on its website?
options: Within one month after the year ends
Within six months after the annual GMS
Within four months after the year ends
Only when OJK asks for it
cards.explanation: Article 131 requires the governance report to be submitted to OJK and the controlling shareholder, and published on the bank's website, no later than four months after the financial year ends.

cards.back: Rapat Umum Pemegang Saham: the General Meeting of Shareholders (GMS).
The Board of Directors, which manages the bank and is fully responsible for that management.
The Board of Commissioners, which supervises and advises the directors.
An independent commissioner: no financial, management, shareholding or family ties that could affect independent judgement.
An independent party from outside the bank who can sit on certain commissioner committees.
Self-assessment of governance, done at least twice a year and included in the governance report.

cards.title: Stage 1 take-aways
items: POJK 17/2023 (in force 14 September 2023) is the umbrella governance rule for Indonesian commercial banks and revoked POJK 55/2016.
Good governance rests on five principles: transparency, accountability, responsibility, independence and fairness.
Directors manage; commissioners supervise and advise and stay out of operational decisions, with narrow exceptions.
Self-assess governance at least twice a year; file and publish the governance report within four months of year-end.
SEOJK 14/2025 scores governance on 16 factors across structure, process and outcome.

cards.prompt: Think of a decision your unit took recently. Which of the five governance principles did it test most, and what evidence would show OJK that the principle was respected?

quiz.question: Which statement correctly describes the status of POJK 17/2023 when it was issued?
options: It took effect one year later and only amended POJK 55/2016
It applies only to banks listed on the stock exchange
It took effect on promulgation and revoked POJK 55/2016
It is guidance that banks may adopt voluntarily
quiz.explanation: POJK 17/2023 was set and promulgated on 14 September 2023, took effect on promulgation, and Article 142 revoked POJK 55/POJK.03/2016 on governance for commercial banks.

quiz.question: A new director at Bank Rinjani Raya asks which body supervises the directors' management of the bank and advises them. What is the correct answer?
options: The General Meeting of Shareholders
The compliance unit
The risk management committee
The Board of Commissioners
quiz.explanation: Under POJK 17/2023 the Board of Commissioners supervises the policies and conduct of management by the directors and gives them advice. The compliance unit and the directors' risk management committee report within management.

quiz.question: During a credit review, a commissioner wants to approve a large loan to an unrelated corporate borrower personally because 'commissioners should be hands-on'. What does POJK 17/2023 say?
options: They may approve any loan above a size threshold set by the board
They may not join operational decisions, save narrow cases such as related-party funding
They must co-sign every large loan together with the responsible director
They may join if the directors agree to it in writing beforehand
quiz.explanation: Article 49(6) bars commissioners from operational decision-making, except funding to related parties under OJK's lending-limit rules and matters set in the articles or law. Even then directors remain responsible for management.

quiz.question: Which of these is one of the sixteen aspects in which POJK 17/2023 says good governance must show?
options: Anti-fraud strategy, including anti-bribery
Annual market share targets for each region
Branch network expansion plans and timelines
Dividend payout targets
quiz.explanation: Article 2(4) lists sixteen aspects, including the anti-fraud strategy with anti-bribery, sustainable finance, conflicts of interest, remuneration and the work of the boards and committees. Commercial targets are not among them.

quiz.question: Lestari plans the governance self-assessment cycle for next year. What is the minimum frequency she must schedule?
options: Once a year, at financial year-end, before the annual GMS
Twice a year, in step with the soundness rating periods
Every quarter, before each scheduled OJK supervisory meeting
Only when OJK announces a review
quiz.explanation: Article 132 requires a self-assessment of good governance at least twice a year, and the elucidation links the periods to bank soundness rating periods. The results are an integral part of the governance report.

quiz.question: Bank Rinjani Raya sends its governance report to OJK on time but forgets to publish it on its website until five months after year-end. How is this treated?
options: It is late; after one more month it counts as not published
There is no breach, because OJK itself received the report on time
Website publication is optional for banks whose shares are not listed
Only the controlling shareholder can raise the issue
quiz.explanation: Article 131 requires both submission and website publication within four months after year-end. Acting within one month after that deadline is 'late'; beyond it, the bank is treated as not having submitted or published.

quiz.question: A bank has already received a written reprimand for breaching POJK 17/2023's governance duties and the breach continues. Which further sanction does the regulation list?
options: Automatic revocation of the bank's licence
A lower governance factor in the bank's soundness rating
Imprisonment of the director in charge of compliance
Suspension of deposit insurance cover for the bank's customers
quiz.explanation: After a written reprimand, the bank can face a ban on new products, freezing of certain activities, a ban on expansion or new activities, and/or a lower governance factor in its soundness rating. Main parties may also be barred under OJK's reassessment rules, and fines can apply.

quiz.question: OJK finds a serious governance breach. Which range of administrative fine does POJK 17/2023 allow against the bank and/or its controlling shareholder for each violation?
options: From Rp50 million up to Rp500 million
From Rp500 million up to Rp5 billion
From Rp10 billion up to Rp100 billion
From Rp2 billion up to Rp50 billion
quiz.explanation: The sanction articles of POJK 17/2023, such as Article 5(4), allow a fine of at least Rp2 billion and at most Rp50 billion for each violation, in addition to other administrative sanctions.

quiz.question: Yosef asks how SEOJK 14/2025 groups the assessment of governance. What should you tell him?
options: Into strategy, sales and operations
Into first, second and third lines of defence
Into structure, process and outcome
Into credit, market and liquidity risk
quiz.explanation: OJK's FAQ on SEOJK 14/SEOJK.03/2025 explains that the assessment rests on the five principles and is grouped into three aspects: structure, process and outcome, across 16 factors.

quiz.question: After the 2023 rule was announced, a controlling shareholder told the board to approve an unsound related deal 'because we own the bank'. Which message from OJK's announcement is most relevant?
options: Owners must not push the bank into acts that breach OJK rules
Owners may direct daily operations once they hold a majority of shares
OJK only supervises directors and commissioners, not the owners
Owners can overrule commissioners on related deals
quiz.explanation: OJK's September 2023 press release stressed that controlling shareholders should not issue policies, take decisions or act towards the bank in breach of OJK rules or the law, or manage it unsoundly. POJK 17/2023 sets clearer limits on shareholder behaviour.

sessions.title: The Boards: Directors, Commissioners and Conflicts of Interest
sessions.summary: Learn the composition, independence, meeting and conduct rules for both boards, OJK's role when the president director or compliance director is removed early, and how to handle conflicts of interest and dissent.
objectives: Check board composition, domicile, experience and terms against POJK 17/2023
Apply independence, cooling-off and term rules for independent commissioners
Identify concurrent positions, shareholdings and benefits that directors may not hold
Handle a conflict of interest and record dissent correctly in minutes
Explain when commissioners must alert OJK

cards.title: Pressure from the owner
cards.setting: Corporate Secretary's office, Jakarta. Wednesday, 4:40 pm.

lines.text: I've just had a call from our controlling shareholder's office. They want two items on the agenda of next month's GMS.
First: remove Hendra as compliance director before his term ends. Second: appoint their former group finance chief, who left our bank's board four months ago, as an independent commissioner.
Is this because I objected to the loan to their property affiliate? I put my dissent in the minutes.
Whatever the reason, neither item can simply be voted through. OJK has a say in both.
And the nomination committee hasn't even met on either name.
Stage two: the Two Tables. Let's learn the rules for each board before anyone drafts a GMS notice.

cards.title: Who may sit on the Board of Directors

scenes.heading: At least three
scenes.narration: A commercial bank must have at least three directors, and every one of them must live in Indonesia. One is appointed president director.

scenes.heading: Experience and terms
scenes.narration: A majority of directors need at least five years' operational experience as executive officers of a bank. Each term lasts at most five years, as set in the articles of association.

scenes.heading: An independent leader
scenes.narration: The president director must be independent of the controlling shareholder. Appointments and replacements put to the GMS must take account of the nomination committee's recommendation.

scenes.heading: OJK approval and conduct
scenes.narration: Every director must meet OJK's approval requirements before taking office, and while in office must keep integrity, competence and a good reputation.

scenes.heading: Removal is not a weapon
scenes.narration: Removing a director early must serve the bank's main interest and rest on an objective assessment, not on a shareholder's subjective view. For the president director and the compliance director, OJK must approve first.

cards.title: The two boards side by side
cards.caption: Articles 6, 7, 17, 30, 35, 36, 38, 47 and 55 of POJK 17/2023.

items.label: Minimum size
items.right: At least 3, and no more than the number of directors

items.label: Domicile
items.right: At least 1 member lives in Indonesia

items.label: Leader
items.left: President director, independent of the controlling shareholder

items.label: Independence
items.left: Majority not related to each other within the second degree

items.label: Meetings
items.left: At least monthly; with commissioners at least every 4 months
items.right: At least every 2 months; all members in person at least twice a year

cards.question: The controlling shareholder wants to replace the compliance director before his term ends. What must happen first?
options: The GMS votes, then the bank tells OJK within a month
The board of commissioners approves it by majority
The nomination committee approves it, with no OJK role
OJK must approve the plan before the GMS decides it
cards.explanation: Article 11 requires prior OJK approval before a GMS decides to remove or replace the president director or the director in charge of compliance before the term ends. The bank applies at least one month before the planned GMS; if OJK finds the plan unfit, the item may not go on the agenda.

cards.title: Independent commissioners
cards.body:
At least **50 percent** of the Board of Commissioners must be **independent commissioners**: people with no financial, management, shareholding or family ties to the directors, other commissioners or the controlling shareholder, nor any link to the bank that could affect their independence.

- Candidates need **adequate banking knowledge** and **banking or finance experience**.
- **Cooling-off:** a former director, executive officer or other party linked to the bank waits **at least one year** before becoming an independent commissioner of that bank. The wait is **at least six months** for a former president director, or a director or executive officer who ran a supervisory function there.
- A non-independent commissioner who wants to switch also waits **one year** and needs OJK approval through fit and proper assessment.
- Independent commissioners serve at most **two consecutive terms**, unless re-appointment is backed by performance and independence assessments and their own statement to the GMS.
- They **may not hold a public office** at the same time.

cards.title: Allowed or prohibited for a director?
cards.prompt: Under POJK 17/2023, sort what a member of Bank Rinjani Raya's Board of Directors may and may not do.

items.text: Serve on the board of commissioners of a non-bank subsidiary the bank controls, with commissioners' approval
Sit on the board of a nonprofit foundation, reported to the commissioners' meeting
Use an independent expert under a clear contract for a defined special project
Act as a director of another company at the same time
Own 30 percent of another company's paid-up capital
Give a general power of attorney that hands over the director's duties
Take personal benefits from the bank beyond remuneration set by the GMS
Keep a personal adviser on retainer who also makes operational decisions

cards.title: Real case: governance failure ends a bank (2026)
cards.body:
On **9 February 2026** OJK's Cirebon office announced that it had revoked the licence of **Perumda BPR Bank Cirebon**, a conventional rural bank owned by a regional government in West Java.

- OJK said it had found **serious problems in governance and in the integrity of the bank's management**, including actions that ignored prudence, good governance, adequate risk management and compliance, which badly hurt the bank's finances.
- OJK stepped up supervision, imposed administrative sanctions and orders, ran a **comprehensive evaluation of management performance**, and oversaw a recovery plan.
- On 2 August 2024 the bank was placed in recovery status (capital ratio below 12 percent, rated unsound) and on 1 August 2025 in resolution status, after its management and shareholders failed to fix it.
- The deposit insurer, LPS, decided not to rescue it and asked OJK to revoke the licence; LPS then pays guaranteed deposits and liquidates the bank.

**Lesson:** weak boards and owners can end a bank. Rural banks have their own governance rules, but the warning applies to every bank.

cards.title: Minutes, dissent and a conflict
cards.setting: Board of Directors meeting, Jakarta. Monday, 9:00 am.

lines.text: Item three: the credit line for Graha Teluk, a property company owned by our controlling shareholder's family.
Before you discuss it: Pak Rudi, our director of business, sits on Graha Teluk's supervisory board through a family holding. He hasn't declared it.
Then he has a conflict of interest, and the decision is already exposed.
Joining by video. Remember, this is funding to a related party. It also needs the commissioners' involvement under the lending-limit rules.
And whatever is decided, every dissent goes into the minutes with its reasons.

cards.title: The undeclared conflict
cards.situation: In the board meeting, Pak Rudi, director of business, is about to present and vote on a credit line for a company where he sits on the supervisory board through a family holding. He has not disclosed this. The president director looks at you, the analyst taking notes. What is the best course?

choices.text: Ask the chair to pause the item, have Pak Rudi disclose the conflict, record it and keep him out of the decision.
choices.outcome: Best. Article 80 requires board members, committee members, executive officers and staff to avoid conflicts of interest and to disclose them in every decision where one exists, and bans actions that could harm the bank. The minutes must record it, and the related-party process still applies.

choices.text: Let him present but note privately that he should abstain from the vote.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Abstaining helps, but the duty is to disclose the conflict in the decision itself. A private note leaves no record and he still shapes the discussion.

choices.text: Say nothing: the loan has been priced at market rates, so there is no harm.
choices.outcome: Poor. Disclosure is required whenever a conflict exists, not only when harm is proven. Silence also breaches the bank's conflict of interest policy and exposes the decision.

choices.text: Tell the controlling shareholder's office so they can decide whether he votes.
choices.outcome: Poor. Conflicts are managed inside the bank's governance, not by the shareholder whose affiliate benefits. That would make the conflict worse.

cards.title: Handling a conflict of interest
cards.caption: Articles 31, 32, 57 and 80 of POJK 17/2023. Every bank must also have a written conflict of interest policy to identify, reduce and manage conflicts.

items.label: Spot it
items.detail: Financial, family, management or ownership links to a decision, customer or supplier.

items.label: Disclose it
items.detail: Declare it in the decision where it arises, before discussion starts.

items.label: Step back
items.detail: Do not take actions that could harm the bank or reduce its profit.

items.label: Record it
items.detail: Minutes show the disclosure, who decided and any dissent with reasons.

items.label: Report it
items.detail: Shareholdings of 5% or more and financial or family ties appear in the governance report.

cards.back: A director may not own, alone or jointly, 25 percent or more of another company's paid-up capital (bonus shares are an exception).
A majority of directors may not be related within the second degree to each other or to commissioners; the same applies to commissioners.
At least once a month, and with the commissioners at least once every four months, quorate with a majority present.
Report to OJK within 5 working days of finding a breach of financial or banking law, or a threat to the bank's survival.
Taken first by deliberation for consensus; failing that, by majority vote. Dissent is minuted with reasons.
Former OJK or other regulator staff wait at least 6 months after leaving before joining a bank's board.

cards.title: Real case: an international review widens related-party scrutiny (2025)
cards.body:
Indonesia's financial sector was reviewed under the **Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP)** of the IMF and the World Bank, which tests banking supervision against the Basel Core Principles.

- OJK's FAQ on circular **SEOJK 14/SEOJK.03/2025** (in force 24 June 2025) explains that its concept of **parties with a special relationship** (pihak yang memiliki hubungan istimewa) follows up an FSAP finding on **Core Principle 20**, which deals with transactions with related parties.
- OJK states that this concept is **wider** than the 'related parties' defined in its legal lending limit rules for commercial banks.
- The same circular introduced the 16-factor self-assessment worksheet that banks first used for the December 2025 position.

**Lesson:** when you check a board decision for conflicts, do not stop at the related-party list used for lending limits. Ask who else has a special relationship with the bank or its leaders.

cards.question: Yosef learns that a director has been booking fictitious loans to cover losses. Under POJK 17/2023, what must the Board of Commissioners do?
options: Report it to OJK within five working days of finding it
Wait for internal audit's annual report before acting
Ask the controlling shareholder to decide on the next step
Report it to OJK at the next annual governance report
cards.explanation: Article 51 requires the Board of Commissioners to report to OJK within five working days of finding a breach of financial or banking laws, or a situation that could endanger the bank's continuity.

cards.title: Writing minutes that protect the bank
cards.body:
- Record **who attended** and whether the meeting was quorate (a majority of members).
- Capture **disclosures of conflicts** at the start of the item, not afterwards.
- Record **dissent with its reasons**: POJK 17/2023 requires it for board and committee meetings.
- For strategic decisions, show the decision was taken **in a meeting**, by consensus first and then by majority.
- File minutes so that OJK examiners and the audit committee can trace decisions later.

cards.title: Stage 2 take-aways
items: At least three directors, all living in Indonesia, a president director independent of the controlling shareholder, terms of up to five years.
Removing the president director or compliance director before term needs OJK approval before the GMS decides.
At least half the commissioners are independent; cooling-off periods and term limits protect that independence.
Directors face limits on other positions, shareholdings of 25% or more, family ties and personal benefits.
Disclose conflicts of interest in every affected decision and record dissent in the minutes.
Commissioners report serious breaches or threats to OJK within five working days.

cards.prompt: If you sat on a board that disagreed with its controlling shareholder, what would you rely on (rules, minutes, committees, OJK) to keep the decision in the bank's interest?

quiz.question: Bank Rinjani Raya's board currently has three directors. One moves abroad and plans to keep serving from Singapore. Which requirement does this break?
options: A majority of directors must live in Jakarta
All directors must live in Indonesia
Only the president director must live in Indonesia
Directors abroad need commissioners' approval
quiz.explanation: Article 6(2) requires every member of the Board of Directors to be domiciled in Indonesia. For commissioners, only at least one member must be.

quiz.question: Which statement about the president director of a commercial bank is correct?
options: The president director must be nominated by OJK
The president director chairs the audit committee of the commissioners
The president director may also serve as president commissioner of the bank
The president director must be independent of the controlling shareholder
quiz.explanation: Article 7(3) requires the president director to come from a party independent of the controlling shareholder.

quiz.question: The Board of Commissioners has six members. What is the minimum number of independent commissioners?
options: Three
Two
Four
One
quiz.explanation: Article 38(2) requires independent commissioners to make up at least 50 percent of the Board of Commissioners. Half of six is three.

quiz.question: A director left Bank Rinjani Raya's board, where he ran the business division, four months ago. The owner wants him as an independent commissioner of the same bank now. What applies?
options: He must wait at least one year after leaving
He can start at once if the GMS agrees
He must wait at least three years after leaving
He can start once OJK approves his shares
quiz.explanation: Article 38(4) sets a waiting period of at least one year for former directors or executive officers before becoming an independent commissioner of the same bank. The shorter six-month wait applies only to a former president director or a director or officer who ran a supervisory function.

quiz.question: The bank wants to remove its president director before the end of his term. When must it apply to OJK?
options: Within one month after the GMS has taken its final decision
At least one month before the GMS that will decide it
At least six months before the GMS
Only if the director objects to removal
quiz.explanation: Article 11(4) requires the application, with reasons, to reach OJK at least one month before the planned GMS. If OJK judges the plan unfit, the item may not be put on the GMS agenda.

quiz.question: Which of these is a director of a commercial bank allowed to do under POJK 17/2023?
options: Serve as a director of one of the bank's suppliers
Hold a functional role at another bank abroad, if paid modestly
Give a general power of attorney to his deputy for his whole portfolio
Be a commissioner of a non-bank subsidiary the bank controls
quiz.explanation: Article 15(2) excludes from the concurrent-position ban a director who oversees the bank's equity participation and serves as commissioner of a controlled non-bank subsidiary. This needs approval from the commissioners' meeting.

quiz.question: How often must the Board of Commissioners meet, at minimum?
options: Every month, with at least one member attending in person
Every quarter, with the president commissioner always present
Every two months; all in person at least twice a year
Twice a year, both meetings held in person
quiz.explanation: Article 55 requires commissioners' meetings at least once every two months, joint meetings with the directors at least once every four months, and physical attendance by all commissioners at least twice a year.

quiz.question: In a directors' meeting, the compliance director disagrees with a decision to restructure a related-party loan. The majority approves it. What must the minutes show?
options: Only the final decision, to protect board unity
The dissent, but only if the director asks
The dissent and the reasons for it
Nothing until the commissioners review the loan
quiz.explanation: Article 31(5) requires any difference of opinion in a directors' meeting to be stated clearly in the minutes together with the reasons. Similar rules apply to commissioners' and committee meetings.

quiz.question: A director discovers he holds a family stake in a borrower whose loan the board will decide today. What does POJK 17/2023 require of him?
options: Disclose it in the next annual governance report and then vote as normal
Disclose the conflict in that decision and avoid harming the bank
Ask the borrower to withdraw the application until next year
Nothing, if the loan is below his approval limit
quiz.explanation: Article 80 requires board members, committee members, executive officers and staff to disclose conflicts of interest in each decision where one exists and bars them from actions that could harm the bank or reduce its profit.

quiz.question: In the Cirebon rural bank case announced by OJK in February 2026, which finding did OJK report before revoking the licence?
options: Serious governance and management integrity problems
A cyber attack that wiped out the bank's customer records
Fraud by an outsourced debt collector
A failed merger with a commercial bank
quiz.explanation: OJK's Cirebon office said it had found serious problems in governance and management integrity, including actions inconsistent with prudence, governance, risk management and compliance, which significantly affected the bank's finances.

sessions.title: Committees and Fit and Proper Leadership
sessions.summary: Rebuild the directors' and commissioners' committees to OJK's minimum standards, understand the role of independent parties and the nomination cycle, and see in general terms how OJK's fit and proper assessment guards the boardroom.
objectives: List the minimum committees of the directors and of the commissioners
Check committee membership, chairing, meeting frequency and charter reviews
Explain the role of independent parties and their certification needs
Describe fit and proper assessment in general terms and the role of the nomination committee

cards.title: Three committees, one empty chair
cards.setting: Commissioners' meeting room, Jakarta. Thursday, 2:00 pm.

lines.text: Bad news. The independent party on my risk monitoring committee, our risk expert, resigned yesterday. And his risk management certificate had lapsed anyway.
Then the committee no longer meets its minimum membership. And the audit committee chair has just been asked to chair the remuneration and nomination committee too.
Speaking of nomination: the shareholder's candidate for independent commissioner still needs a recommendation from our committee, and then OJK's fit and proper assessment.
And a director's committee question: our IT steering committee hasn't met since the core banking upgrade.
Stage three: the Committee Rooms. Let's rebuild each committee properly, then look at how OJK judges whether people are fit and proper.

scenes.heading: Two sets of committees
scenes.narration: Directors form committees to support management, and commissioners form committees to support oversight. Each committee answers to the board that created it.

scenes.heading: Directors' committees
scenes.narration: At minimum the directors must have a risk management committee, a credit policy committee, a credit committee and an IT steering committee, and evaluate their performance at least every year-end.

scenes.heading: Commissioners' committees
scenes.narration: At minimum the commissioners must have an audit committee, a risk monitoring committee and a remuneration and nomination committee, which may be split in two.

scenes.heading: Independent voices
scenes.narration: Commissioners' committees are chaired by an independent commissioner, bring in independent experts from outside the bank, and exclude directors from membership.

scenes.heading: Charters and minutes
scenes.narration: Every committee needs a written charter reviewed at least every three years, minutes of each meeting, and dissent recorded with reasons.

cards.title: Who sits on the commissioners' committees
cards.caption: Articles 63 to 67 and 77 of POJK 17/2023, for a conventional commercial bank. The experts are 'independent parties' from outside the bank.

items.label: Audit committee
items.left: 1 independent commissioner (chair), 1 finance or accounting expert, 1 law or banking expert
items.right: All members independent; no directors; meets at least monthly

items.label: Risk monitoring committee
items.left: 1 independent commissioner (chair), 1 risk management expert, 1 finance expert
items.right: Majority independent; experts hold a risk certificate like directors'; meets at least monthly

items.label: Remuneration and nomination
items.left: 1 independent commissioner (chair), 1 non-independent commissioner, HR executive or staff representative
items.right: No directors; if over 3 members, at least 2 independent commissioners; meets at least quarterly

cards.question: Yosef's risk monitoring committee needs a new independent risk expert. What must that expert hold under POJK 17/2023?
options: A law degree recognised by OJK
A banking licence issued by Bank Indonesia
Five years' service at the same bank
A risk management certificate like the one required of directors
cards.explanation: Article 65(3) requires the independent parties on the risk monitoring committee to hold a risk management certificate as required for directors, plus competence certificates that support the committee's work.

cards.title: Which committee does this?
cards.prompt: Match each task with the committee that POJK 17/2023 gives it.

pairs.right: Monitors audit planning and follow-up, and checks financial reports against accounting standards
Checks that risk policy and practice match, and evaluates the risk management unit
Recommends candidates for the boards and runs board performance evaluations
A directors' committee that shapes the bank's lending policy
A directors' committee that steers the bank's technology

cards.title: Fit and proper: the gate and the watch
cards.body:
OJK controls who leads a bank in two ways, described here in general terms:

- **The gate.** Directors and commissioners must meet OJK's approval requirements before they take office. OJK's **fit and proper assessment** (penilaian kemampuan dan kepatutan) looks at a candidate's **integrity, competence and reputation**. For candidate directors and commissioners, holding a **risk management certificate** is one aspect of the competence factor.
- **The watch.** Once in office, directors and commissioners must keep their **integrity, competence and good reputation** for as long as they serve. OJK can **reassess** a serving main party, and a bank that ignores governance sanctions can see its main parties barred under OJK's reassessment rules.
- **The bank's part.** The nomination committee recommends candidates, who disclose conflicts of interest during the assessment.

Detailed procedures sit in OJK's separate fit and proper rules; check the current text.

cards.title: The candidate on the fast track
cards.setting: HR director's office, Jakarta. Friday, 11:00 am.

lines.text: The shareholder's candidate for independent commissioner has a strong finance career but no risk management certificate yet.
SEOJK 28/2022 has an accelerated route for exactly this: a fast-track competence test at a banking certification body, for people nominated as directors or commissioners.
He'll need a letter signed by a director, plus either the GMS resolution or our nomination committee's recommendation.
And he gets one fast-track attempt only. If he fails, he goes through the normal tiered route.
There's another catch. He left our board four months ago. As an independent commissioner, he faces a cooling-off period first.

cards.title: Filling the risk monitoring committee
cards.situation: The risk monitoring committee now has two members: Yosef (independent commissioner, chair) and an independent finance expert. A director of the bank offers to sit on it 'temporarily' because he knows risk well. Another option is a retired risk professor with a valid risk management certificate and no ties to the bank. What should Lestari recommend to the commissioners?

choices.text: Appoint the retired professor through the directors, based on the commissioners' meeting decision and the nomination committee's advice.
choices.outcome: Best. Directors may not sit on the risk monitoring committee. It needs an independent risk expert who holds a risk management certificate like directors'. Committee members are appointed by the directors on the basis of a commissioners' meeting decision, and the nomination committee recommends independent parties.

choices.text: Let the director join until a permanent expert is found.
choices.outcome: Poor. POJK 17/2023 expressly bans directors from being members of the risk monitoring committee, even for a short time. It would also undermine the committee's independence over management.

choices.text: Keep the committee at two members and record the vacancy in the governance report.
choices.outcome: Partly right: transparency helps, but the committee no longer meets the minimum membership. The bank must act to fill the gap, not only disclose it.

choices.text: Ask the controlling shareholder to nominate one of its own executives.
choices.outcome: Poor. An executive of the controlling shareholder is not an independent party, so the committee would fail the independence test.

cards.title: The nomination cycle
cards.caption: Articles 9, 38, 41 and 73 of POJK 17/2023 and Section III of SEOJK 28/2022.

items.label: Policy
items.detail: The remuneration and nomination committee designs selection and replacement procedures.

items.label: Candidates
items.detail: It identifies and recommends candidates to the commissioners for the GMS.

items.label: OJK assessment
items.detail: Candidates face fit and proper assessment and disclose conflicts of interest.

items.label: Appointment
items.detail: The GMS appoints, taking account of the committee's recommendation.

items.label: Evaluation
items.detail: The committee assesses the boards' performance, feeding the next cycle.

cards.title: Fixing the committee line-up
cards.prompt: Put Bank Rinjani Raya's steps to restore its commissioners' committees in a sensible order.
steps: Map each committee's current members against POJK 17/2023's minimum composition
Ask the remuneration and nomination committee to recommend suitable independent parties
Decide the appointments in a commissioners' meeting
Have the directors formally appoint the members, based on that decision
Update each committee charter and set the meeting calendar
Report the composition and meetings in the governance report

cards.question: The audit committee chair is asked to chair the remuneration and nomination committee as well. Is that allowed?
options: No, a committee chair may never sit on another committee
Yes, but chairing more than one other committee is barred
Only if OJK approves it in advance
Yes, with no limit on how many committees one person chairs
cards.explanation: Article 70 bars the chair of a commissioners' committee from also chairing more than one other committee. Chairing the audit committee and one other committee stays within that limit.

cards.title: Real case: OJK's ethics and risk culture guide (2026)
cards.body:
In its press release of **5 November 2026** (SP 219/OJK/DKPU/XI/2026) on the October 2026 Board of Commissioners meeting, OJK reported that it had issued a **Guide to Applying Banking Ethics and Risk Culture for Commercial Banks** (Panduan Penerapan Etika dan Budaya Risiko Perbankan bagi Bank Umum).

- The guide aims to strengthen ethics and risk culture through a practical, structured approach consistent with OJK rules.
- It stresses **integrity and ethics at every level** of the organisation, sound and sustainable risk management, responsible decision-making, and effective internal control and governance.
- It sets out **nine main principles** to guide behaviour and decisions.
- In the same release OJK announced its **banking roadmap for 2026 to 2030 (RP3I)**, whose first strategic priority is strengthening institutions and integrity.

**Lesson:** committees and fit and proper tests are structures; OJK expects them to be backed by a culture in which people at every level act with integrity.

cards.title: OJK's governance yardsticks in numbers
cards.caption: Sources: OJK FAQ on SEOJK 14/SEOJK.03/2025; OJK press release SP 219/OJK/DKPU/XI/2026.

items.label: Governance factors
items.detail: Factors banks score in the self-assessment under SEOJK 14/2025.

items.label: Assessment aspects
items.detail: Governance structure, process and outcome.

items.label: Ethics principles
items.detail: Main principles in OJK's 2026 ethics and risk culture guide for commercial banks.

items.label: Roadmap priorities
items.detail: Strategic priorities of OJK's 2026-2030 banking roadmap, starting with institutions and integrity.

cards.title: Stage 3 take-aways
items: Directors need at least risk management, credit policy, credit and IT steering committees.
Commissioners need at least audit, risk monitoring and remuneration and nomination committees, each chaired by an independent commissioner, with no directors as members.
Independent experts on the risk monitoring committee must hold a risk management certificate like directors'.
Committee charters are reviewed at least every three years; minutes record dissent with reasons.
Fit and proper: OJK approves leaders before they take office and expects integrity, competence and reputation throughout.

cards.prompt: Which committee in your bank do you deal with most? What information do you give it, and how could you make that information more useful for its oversight?

quiz.question: Which committees must the Board of Directors of a commercial bank form at minimum?
options: Audit, risk monitoring, and remuneration and nomination committees, at least
Risk management, credit policy, credit, and IT steering committees
Compliance, marketing, and branch performance committees
Asset-liability, HR, and sustainability committees
quiz.explanation: Article 62(2) of POJK 17/2023 lists the directors' minimum committees: risk management, credit or financing policy, credit or financing, and IT steering. Audit, risk monitoring and remuneration and nomination are commissioners' committees.

quiz.question: Who must chair Bank Rinjani Raya's audit committee?
options: An independent commissioner who is also a member
The director in charge of compliance
An independent party with an accounting background
The head of internal audit
quiz.explanation: Article 64(4) requires the audit committee to be chaired by an independent commissioner who is also a member. Directors are barred from membership.

quiz.question: The bank proposes an audit committee of one independent commissioner, one independent accounting expert and the head of the bank's legal division. What is wrong?
options: Nothing is wrong, as long as the committee chair is an independent commissioner
Every member must be independent, so a bank employee cannot take a seat
The committee also needs the director in charge of compliance as a member
The legal seat must go to a non-independent commissioner
quiz.explanation: Article 64(1) requires all audit committee members to be independent: at least one independent commissioner plus independent parties with finance or accounting expertise and with law or banking expertise. A bank employee is not an independent party.

quiz.question: How often must the risk monitoring committee meet at minimum?
options: Once every two months
Once a month
Once a quarter
Twice a year
quiz.explanation: Article 77(1) requires the audit committee and the risk monitoring committee to meet at least once a month, and the remuneration and nomination committee at least once every three months.

quiz.question: The remuneration and nomination committee is planned with five members. What extra rule applies?
options: At least one director must join as a member
The HR executive must chair it
At least two of them must be independent commissioners
OJK must approve each member in advance
quiz.explanation: Article 66(6) provides that if the remuneration and nomination committee has more than three members, at least two must be independent commissioners. It is chaired by an independent commissioner and directors may not be members.

quiz.question: Bank Rinjani Raya last reviewed its committee charters in 2021. It is now 2026. Which requirement has it missed?
options: Reviewing each committee charter at least once every three years
Reviewing charters only when OJK issues or amends a relevant POJK
Having OJK approve every charter change before it applies
Publishing all charters in a national newspaper each year
quiz.explanation: Article 75(3) requires banks to review the charters of each directors' and commissioners' committee periodically, at least once every three years.

quiz.question: A former executive officer of the bank, who did not hold a supervisory function, wants to be an independent party on the audit committee. What applies?
options: No waiting period, because committees are advisory
A waiting period of at least two years
Approval from the controlling shareholder instead of a wait
A waiting period of at least six months before joining
quiz.explanation: Article 69(1) requires former directors, executive officers and others linked to the bank to wait at least six months before becoming an independent party on the audit or risk monitoring committee. The wait does not apply to those who held a supervisory function.

quiz.question: A candidate director asks what role a risk management certificate plays in OJK's fit and proper assessment. What is accurate?
options: It is one aspect of the competence factor for board candidates
It replaces the integrity assessment entirely for directors
It is only needed after a director has served five years in office
It matters only for directors of listed banks
quiz.explanation: SEOJK 28/2022, Section II point 12, states that holding a risk management certificate is one aspect of the competence factor in the fit and proper assessment of candidate directors and commissioners.

quiz.question: The commissioners decide who will join the risk monitoring committee. Who formally appoints the members?
options: The GMS, on the proposal of the controlling shareholder's representative
OJK, after a fit and proper test of each member
The directors, based on the commissioners' meeting decision
The committee chair, without needing a board decision
quiz.explanation: Article 63(5) requires members of commissioners' committees to be appointed and dismissed by the directors based on a decision of the commissioners' meeting.

quiz.question: In its November 2026 release, which new OJK document for commercial banks focused on integrity, ethics and risk culture at every level?
options: A circular requiring every member of staff to sit an annual ethics exam
A regulation banning performance bonuses for executive officers
A code requiring commissioners to live in Jakarta
An ethics and risk culture guide with nine main principles
quiz.explanation: OJK's press release SP 219/OJK/DKPU/XI/2026 reported the Guide to Applying Banking Ethics and Risk Culture for Commercial Banks, which stresses integrity and ethics across the organisation and sets nine main principles.

sessions.title: Risk Management Certification and Staff Development (SEOJK 28/2022, POJK 24/2022)
sessions.summary: Find out who must hold a risk management certificate, how long it lasts, how recognised refreshers keep it valid, what happens when it lapses, and how the 3.5 percent staff development floor and critical positions work.
objectives: Identify who must hold a valid risk management certificate under SEOJK 28/2022
Keep certificates valid through recognised yearly refreshers or re-certification
Apply the six-month replacement rule and the one-time fast track for board candidates
Calculate and evidence the POJK 24/2022 staff development spending floor
Explain critical positions, outsourced staff duties and monitoring obligations

cards.title: The certificate that nearly lapsed
cards.setting: HR division, Bank Rinjani Raya, Jakarta. Monday, 8:30 am.

lines.text: I've pulled the certification register. Pak Hendra's risk management certificate expires in September. Ibu Sri, our finance director, let hers lapse in March.
Mine is safe, I think. I attended two seminars last year.
Were they recognised by the certification body? And there's more: our Makassar credit officers, including Fajar, aren't in the register at all.
And our training spend. Finance says we spent 2.1 percent of last year's gross salary cost on staff development.
That's below OJK's floor. The risk monitoring committee wants a plan by Friday.
Stage four: the Certification Tower. Let's learn exactly who needs what, and how to keep it valid.

cards.title: Two rules that build a bank's people

scenes.heading: POJK 24 of 2022
scenes.narration: POJK 24 of 2022 on developing the quality of commercial bank human resources took effect on 5 December 2022. It requires banks to manage and develop all their people continuously: directors, commissioners, permanent and temporary staff.

scenes.heading: A spending floor
scenes.narration: Each financial year a bank must provide, and actually spend, at least 3.5 percent of the previous year's total gross salary cost on developing its people.

scenes.heading: Certification by OJK field
scenes.narration: OJK sets fields of banking competency certification. Risk management is one of them; certificates are issued by banking-sector professional certification bodies, called LSP, registered with OJK.

scenes.heading: SEOJK 28 of 2022
scenes.narration: Circular SEOJK 28 of 2022, in force since 22 December 2022, sets the detail for risk management certification: who must hold a certificate, how long it lasts and how refreshers keep it alive.

scenes.heading: Replacing the 2009 regime
scenes.narration: Together they replaced Bank Indonesia's 2009 risk management certification regulation and its 2010 amendment.

cards.title: Who must hold a risk management certificate
cards.caption: SEOJK 28/2022, Section II point 1. Each must hold a valid certificate for as long as they hold the post. Banks may add other staff, such as the legal team, under internal policy.

items.label: Directors
items.detail: Every member of the Board of Directors.

items.label: Commissioners
items.detail: Every member of the Board of Commissioners.

items.label: Executive officers
items.detail: Division heads and above, regional and branch heads, heads of risk, compliance and internal audit.

items.label: Officers in control units
items.detail: Other officers in the risk management, compliance and internal audit units.

items.label: Officers in risk-taking units
items.detail: Other officers in main units that take risk decisions, such as credit, treasury, IT and finance.

cards.question: Fajar is a credit officer below executive level in the Makassar branch's lending unit. Does SEOJK 28/2022 require him to hold a risk management certificate?
options: Yes, as an officer in a main unit that takes credit risk decisions
No, only directors and commissioners need one
No, only staff in the risk management unit need one
Only if he is promoted to branch head
cards.explanation: SEOJK 28/2022 extends the requirement to officers below executive level in the main operating units that take and carry out risk decisions, including credit, treasury, IT and finance, as well as officers in the risk, compliance and internal audit units.

cards.title: Keeping a certificate valid
cards.body:
Under SEOJK 28/2022:

- A risk management certificate is valid for **three years** from its issue date and can be **extended** for another three years from the end of the previous validity.
- Holders follow a **refresher (maintenance) programme at least once every year** after the certificate is issued. Forms include in-house training, seminars, regulator briefings, workshops, e-learning and work portfolios on bank risk management.
- Refreshers **extend** the certificate only if they are held at least yearly, cover bank risk management, and both the programme and its provider are **recognised by the banking-sector certification body (LSP)**.
- If refreshers do not meet these criteria, the holder must **re-certify** to extend.
- The bank must **monitor** that staff take part and keep certificates valid, and the bank and holders must **keep evidence** of certificates and refresher attendance.

cards.title: Counts towards a valid extension?
cards.prompt: Hendra wants his refreshers to extend his certificate. Sort each activity.

items.text: A yearly e-learning module on bank risk management recognised by the LSP
An LSP-recognised workshop on climate-related risk for banks
A regulator's briefing on new risk rules that the LSP recognises
A work portfolio on risk management assessed under LSP criteria
A leadership retreat with no risk management content
A risk seminar from a provider the LSP does not recognise
One refresher in three years, taken just before expiry

cards.title: Real case: from Bank Indonesia's 2009 regime to OJK's 2022 rules
cards.body:
Risk management certification for Indonesian bank leaders is not new.

- **2009-2010:** Bank Indonesia required risk management certificates for bank directors, commissioners and officers through PBI 11/19/PBI/2009, amended by PBI 12/7/PBI/2010, with five certificate levels.
- **5 December 2022:** OJK's POJK 24/2022 took effect, revoked that BI regulation and made it an umbrella for certification in fields OJK sets. OJK's FAQ confirms the new rule strengthens the earlier risk certification regime.
- **22 December 2022:** SEOJK 28/2022 set the details and mapped old levels 1 to 5 onto qualification levels 4 to 7 of the Indonesian National Qualifications Framework (KKNI), based on the national competency standard (SKKNI) for bank risk management.
- Certification content must keep up with **current risks such as cyber security and climate change**.

**Lesson:** a certificate earned years ago under the old scheme may still count, but only within the alignment rules OJK set, and only while it stays valid.

cards.title: Replace, or renew?
cards.setting: Board of Commissioners meeting, Jakarta. Wednesday, 3:00 pm.

lines.text: Ibu Sri's certificate expired in March. She says she's too busy closing the accounts to re-certify this year.
SEOJK 28/2022 is clear. If a director, commissioner or executive officer lets the certificate lapse and makes no effort to restore it, the bank must replace that person.
No later than six months after the certificate expired. During those six months she can still work to restore it.
And OJK can set a different period in special cases, for example if replacing her would disrupt operations, taking into account what she has done to comply.
So we have until September. Let's give her a choice she can't misunderstand.

cards.title: A director without a valid certificate
cards.situation: It is June. The finance director's risk management certificate expired in March. She has not enrolled in re-certification and says year-end closing comes first. The commissioners ask what the bank should do now.

choices.text: Tell her in writing that she must enrol now, track her progress, and prepare for replacement if the certificate is not restored by the six-month deadline.
choices.outcome: Best. SEOJK 28/2022 lets her restore validity within six months of expiry; if she does not and makes no effort, the bank must replace her by then. Written notice, monitoring and a contingency plan meet the bank's duty to monitor certificate validity.

choices.text: Wait until OJK raises it, since she is otherwise competent.
choices.outcome: Poor. The bank has its own duty to monitor that people keep certificates valid, and its own deadline to act. Waiting for OJK turns an HR issue into a compliance breach.

choices.text: Ask OJK at once for an open-ended exemption because she is hard to replace.
choices.outcome: Partly right: OJK can set a different period in certain conditions, such as when replacement would disrupt operations, and weighs the efforts made. But it is not open-ended and she still needs to make a genuine effort.

choices.text: Move her title to 'advisor' while she keeps running finance.
choices.outcome: Poor. Changing the label while she keeps the role defeats the rule and misleads the regulator. It also raises integrity questions for the board.

cards.title: The numbers that matter
cards.caption: SEOJK 28/2022, Sections II and III; POJK 24/2022, Article 4.

items.label: Certificate validity
items.detail: From the issue date; an extension adds 3 years from the end of the previous validity.

items.label: Minimum refreshers
items.detail: At least one recognised refresher in each year after issue.

items.label: Deadline to replace
items.detail: For a director, commissioner or executive officer whose certificate lapses without effort to restore it.

items.label: Development spending floor
items.detail: Of the previous year's total gross salary cost, provided and spent every financial year.

items.label: Fast-track test
items.detail: A board candidate may use the fast-track route once only, at any certification body.

cards.back: Directors, commissioners, permanent staff and temporary staff of the bank.
The expense booked for directors' salaries, other staff salaries and wages, and commissioners' fees.
Expensed costs of certification, training, formal education, mentoring and secondments, including travel, modules, licences and e-libraries.
Capital spending on training facilities booked as fixed assets, and funds for national HR programmes outside the bank.
A director in charge of HR, who may also cover other areas depending on the bank's size and complexity.
Banks must identify critical functions and positions; people in them must have the competence those roles need.
Banks must make sure outsourced workers are competent for the work outsourced; any spending on them counts towards the floor.

cards.title: Building next year's development plan
cards.prompt: Put Putu's steps for meeting POJK 24/2022 in order.
steps: Take last year's total realised gross salary cost from the profit and loss account
Set a development budget of at least 3.5 percent of that figure
Plan technical, non-technical and leadership programmes, including certifications
Put the plan, participant ratios and funding ratio into the bank business plan
Run the programmes and keep records of who attended
Report the actual spending ratio in the business plan realisation report

cards.question: Bank Rinjani Raya's gross salary cost last year was Rp800 billion. What is the minimum it must provide and spend on staff development this year?
options: Rp8 billion
Rp28 billion
Rp35 billion
Rp80 billion
cards.explanation: POJK 24/2022, Article 4, requires at least 3.5 percent of the previous year's total realised gross salary cost. 3.5 percent of Rp800 billion is Rp28 billion, and the bank must both provide and actually spend it.

cards.title: Real case: OJK warns banks about new risks (2022)
cards.body:
On **6 September 2022**, a few months before POJK 24/2022 and SEOJK 28/2022 were issued, OJK's chief executive for banking supervision, Dian Ediana Rae, set out OJK's direction for building a banking system with integrity.

- OJK said it would intervene when needed to make sure banks apply **governance, risk and compliance (GRC)**, integrity and soundness.
- It urged banks not to become **complacent** with good results and to watch risks from **cyber attacks**, increasingly sophisticated **economic crime**, **climate-related risk**, digitalisation, geopolitical tension and global uncertainty.

**Lesson:** the risks OJK named are the same ones SEOJK 28/2022 tells certification bodies to build into risk management certification, such as cyber security and climate change. Refreshers should keep pace with them.

cards.title: Stage 4 take-aways
items: Directors, commissioners, executive officers and officers in control and risk-taking units must hold a valid risk management certificate while in post.
Certificates last three years; LSP-recognised refreshers at least yearly can extend them, otherwise re-certify.
If a director, commissioner or executive officer lets a certificate lapse without effort, the bank must replace them within six months.
Banks must provide and spend at least 3.5% of the prior year's gross salary cost on staff development each year.
Banks must identify critical positions, monitor certificates and refreshers, and keep the evidence.

cards.prompt: Look at your own role. Does it fall into a group that needs a risk management certificate? If so, when does yours expire, and which recognised refresher will you take this year?

quiz.question: How long is a risk management certificate valid under SEOJK 28/2022?
options: Five years from its issue date, with no extension
One year, renewed by an annual exam
For life, once the highest level is reached
Three years from its issue date, and it can be extended
quiz.explanation: Section II point 5 sets a validity of three years from the issue date, extendable; an extension runs for three years after the previous validity ends.

quiz.question: Which group does SEOJK 28/2022 NOT list as required to hold a risk management certificate?
options: Branch tellers with no role in risk decisions
Members of the Board of Commissioners
Officers below executive level in the internal audit unit
Officers in the treasury unit
quiz.explanation: The circular covers directors, commissioners, executive officers, and officers below executive level in risk, compliance and internal audit units and in main risk-taking units such as credit, treasury, IT and finance. Banks may add others under internal policy.

quiz.question: Hendra attended two risk seminars in the past three years, both from a provider the certification body does not recognise. His certificate expires next month. What follows?
options: The seminars cannot extend the certificate, so he must re-certify
The seminars extend it automatically for three years
The certificate extends for one year only
OJK will approve the seminars on request
quiz.explanation: Refreshers extend a certificate only if held at least yearly, on bank risk management, and with programme and provider recognised by the banking LSP. Otherwise they are not recognised and the holder must re-certify.

quiz.question: How often must a certificate holder take part in a refresher programme?
options: At least once in each year after issue
Once every three years, just before expiry
Twice a year, once in each half of the financial year
Only when the bank changes its risk policy
quiz.explanation: SEOJK 28/2022, Section II point 7, requires the maintenance programme to take place periodically, at least once a year after the certificate is issued.

quiz.question: A commissioner's certificate expired in January and he has made no attempt to restore it. By when must the bank replace him, absent any OJK decision?
options: By the end of the financial year
By July, six months after the certificate expired
Immediately, on the day it expired
By the next annual GMS, whenever it falls
quiz.explanation: Section II point 13 requires the bank to replace a director, commissioner or executive officer who lacks a valid certificate and makes no effort to restore it, no later than six months after expiry. OJK may set another period in certain conditions.

quiz.question: A candidate director fails the fast-track risk management competence test at one certification body. What can she do next?
options: Retake the fast track at the same body after three months
Take the fast track once more at another certification body
Take the normal tiered test; no more fast track anywhere
Ask OJK to waive the certificate for her
quiz.explanation: SEOJK 28/2022, Section III, allows the fast track only once. A candidate found not competent may take the normal tiered test but may not use the fast track again at the same or another banking LSP.

quiz.question: Bank Rinjani Raya's gross salary cost last year was Rp1.2 trillion. It budgets Rp45 billion for staff development but actually spends Rp38 billion. Has it met POJK 24/2022?
options: Yes, because the budget exceeded Rp42 billion
No: the floor is Rp42 billion and it must actually be spent
Yes, because the floor is 3 percent, or Rp36 billion
No: the floor is 5 percent, or Rp60 billion
quiz.explanation: Article 4 requires banks both to provide and to realise at least 3.5 percent of the previous year's total realised gross salary cost. 3.5 percent of Rp1.2 trillion is Rp42 billion; spending Rp38 billion falls short even though the budget was large enough.

quiz.question: Which item can count towards the POJK 24/2022 development spending floor?
options: A new training centre building booked as a fixed asset
Scholarships for a national programme outside the bank
E-library subscriptions and training modules booked as expenses
Salaries of HR staff who run payroll
quiz.explanation: The elucidation of Article 4 includes expensed costs of certification, training, formal education, mentoring, secondments, travel, modules, licences and e-library subscriptions, but excludes capital spending on training facilities booked as fixed assets. Article 21 excludes national HR programme funds.

quiz.question: OJK finds that Bank Rinjani Raya never identified its critical positions. What can OJK do under POJK 24/2022 after a written reprimand if the breach continues?
options: Revoke the approvals of all directors at once, without any hearing
Impose prison terms on the director in charge of HR
Take over the bank's HR function directly
Ban new activities, freeze some activities or cut the soundness rating
quiz.explanation: Article 10 sanctions breaches such as failing to identify critical functions and positions with a written reprimand, then a ban on new business activities, freezing of certain activities and/or a lower soundness rating.

quiz.question: The bank uses outsourced staff for its call centre. What does POJK 24/2022 require?
options: Certify every outsourced worker in risk management before they start
Ensure outsourced staff are competent for the outsourced work
Nothing: outsourced staff fall wholly outside the bank's duties
Spend 3.5 percent of their wages on them
quiz.explanation: Article 5 lets banks choose whether to develop outsourced staff, but requires them to ensure outsourced workers have the competence the outsourced work needs. Any spending on them counts towards the development floor.

sessions.title: Whistleblowing under the Anti-Fraud Strategy and OJK Readiness
sessions.summary: Set up and use a trusted whistleblowing channel under POJK 12/2024, protect reporters from retaliation, route reports to independent investigators, and pull governance, certification and anti-fraud evidence together for OJK's review.
objectives: Place whistleblowing within the four pillars of the POJK 12/2024 anti-fraud strategy
Describe the protections, channels and rewards a whistleblowing system must offer
Route a report to independent, competent investigators and prevent retaliation
Assemble the evidence OJK expects on governance, certification, development spending and anti-fraud

cards.title: Fajar's report
cards.setting: Video call between Makassar and Jakarta. Tuesday, 7:30 pm.

lines.text: I've waited a week to say this. A loan file I processed was approved after the borrower gave my branch manager an envelope. The collateral valuation was also changed after the site visit.
If I report it and I'm wrong, or if he finds out, my career here is over.
