Thank you for trusting us, Fajar. You don't have to prove it. That's what our whistleblowing channel and the anti-fraud unit are for.
Under OJK's anti-fraud regulation, POJK 12 of 2024, you can report through the channel, even anonymously, and the bank must keep your identity confidential and protect you from retaliation.
And the anti-fraud unit has a direct reporting line to the commissioners, so this cannot be buried in the branch.
Final stage: the Safe Channel. Then we pull everything together for OJK's review.

scenes.heading: One regulation for all
scenes.narration: POJK 12 of 2024 requires every financial services institution, commercial banks included, to have and apply an anti-fraud strategy. It took effect three months after promulgation, at the end of October 2024, and replaced the earlier bank-only rule.

scenes.heading: Four pillars
scenes.narration: The strategy has four pillars: prevention; detection; investigation, reporting and sanctions; and monitoring, evaluation and follow-up. Whistleblowing sits in the detection pillar.

scenes.heading: A clear policy
scenes.narration: The bank's whistleblowing policy must be clear, easy to understand and workable, so that staff and outsiders feel encouraged to report fraud.

scenes.heading: Protection
scenes.narration: The bank must protect reporters fully: keep their identity confidential, examine and follow up their reports, and forbid retaliation. Anonymous reports must be possible.

scenes.heading: Recognition
scenes.narration: The bank should also have a way to reward reporters whose reports prove true and are backed by adequate evidence.

cards.title: The four pillars of the anti-fraud strategy
cards.caption: POJK 12/2024, Article 5 and Attachment I.

items.label: Prevention
items.detail: Awareness, risk identification and know-your-employee checks in hiring, promotion and transfers.

items.label: Detection
items.detail: Whistleblowing channel, surprise audits and covert surveillance testing.

items.label: Investigation, reporting, sanctions
items.detail: Independent, competent investigation; reporting inside the bank and to OJK; fair, deterrent sanctions.

items.label: Monitoring, evaluation, follow-up
items.detail: Track cases and fixes, evaluate weak controls, improve the strategy.

cards.question: Under POJK 12/2024, which of these counts as fraud of the 'corruption' type?
options: A cyber attack by an outside hacker group
A loan that defaults after a fall in commodity prices
Accepting an illegal gratuity to approve a loan
A data entry error in a deposit account
cards.explanation: Article 2 classes corruption as including harmful conflicts of interest, bribery, illegal gratuities and extortion. Other fraud types are asset misappropriation, financial statement fraud, deception and leaking confidential information.

cards.title: What a good whistleblowing system contains
cards.body:
POJK 12/2024's guidance on the detection pillar expects at least:

- **Whistleblower protection:** a commitment to open communication channels, full support and protection for reporters, **confidential identity**, proper examination and disclosure of reports, and a **ban on retaliation**. **Anonymous** reporting is possible.
- **Rewards** for reporters whose reports prove true with adequate evidence.
- **Internal rules** on fraud complaints, consistent with the law.
- An **effective reporting system** with a clear process, follow-up mechanism, channels and people responsible. Channels may include a website, messaging apps, phone, letter, email or fax.
- **Transparent communication** of the policy to everyone in the bank and to outsiders, applied consistently so people trust that the channel is reliable and confidential.

The anti-fraud unit or function answers to a director and has a **direct communication and reporting line to the Board of Commissioners**.

cards.title: Match the term to its meaning
cards.prompt: Link each anti-fraud term from POJK 12/2024 to what it means for Bank Rinjani Raya.

pairs.right: Channels and procedures for staff and outsiders to report suspected fraud
Unannounced checks on high-risk units to keep staff alert
Covert testing of whether anti-fraud controls work
Screening and monitoring staff integrity in hiring, promotion and transfers
An event the bank must report to OJK under the regulation's guidance

cards.title: Real case: OJK puts anti-fraud at the centre (2024)
cards.body:
On **14 September 2024**, OJK issued press release SP 138/GKPB/OJK/IX/2024 after its Audit Board chair, Sophia Wattimena, spoke at the Association of Certified Fraud Examiners' Asia Pacific fraud conference.

- OJK said it was strengthening the resilience of the financial sector against rising fraud risk by tightening **anti-fraud regulation**, promoting **good governance**, and using **supervisory technology and artificial intelligence** in supervision.
- It named POJK 12/2024 as an integrated anti-fraud rule for the whole financial sector, alongside POJK 17/2023 on bank governance and POJK 8/2023 on AML, CFT and proliferation financing.
- OJK called for collaboration between itself, industry, law enforcement and government to detect, prevent and respond to fraud.

**Lesson:** OJK reads governance, anti-fraud and AML as one system. A whistleblowing channel that works is evidence that all three are alive.

lines.text: Fajar's report is logged with a case number. The branch manager doesn't know who reported it.
Who investigates? The regional audit team reports to the same regional head as the branch manager.
Then they're not independent. POJK 12/2024 expects investigators chosen for independence and competence: analysis, forensic accounting, computer forensics, fieldwork and interviews.
And the branch manager just asked HR to transfer Fajar to a remote sub-branch. 'Performance reasons', he says.

cards.title: A transfer request after a report
cards.situation: Two days after Fajar's confidential report, his branch manager, who is the subject of the report, asks HR to transfer Fajar to a remote sub-branch for 'performance reasons'. Fajar's file shows good ratings. What should Putu, as head of HR, do?

choices.text: Put the transfer on hold, alert the anti-fraud unit, and protect Fajar's identity while the investigation runs.
choices.outcome: Best. POJK 12/2024 expects full protection for reporters, confidentiality and a ban on retaliation. A sudden adverse move requested by the person reported looks like retaliation; holding it and escalating protects both Fajar and the integrity of the case.

choices.text: Approve the transfer: managers decide staffing, and HR cannot know about the report.
choices.outcome: Poor. Approving an unjustified move against a reporter is exactly the retaliation the policy must forbid, and it would destroy staff trust in the channel.

choices.text: Ask Fajar whether he wants to withdraw his report to avoid the transfer.
choices.outcome: Poor. That pressures the reporter and undermines the whistleblowing system. The bank must follow up reports, not bargain them away.

choices.text: Approve it but give Fajar an extra allowance as compensation.
choices.outcome: Partly wrong. Compensation does not cure retaliation. The issue is whether the move is linked to the report; it should be stopped and reviewed.

cards.title: From report to closure
cards.prompt: Put the handling of a whistleblowing report in a sensible order.
steps: Receive the report through any channel, including anonymously, and log it
Protect the reporter's identity and check for any sign of retaliation
Assign investigators chosen for independence and competence
Report results inside the bank and, where required, to OJK
Apply sanctions fairly and consistently, and fix the weak control
Monitor follow-up and update the anti-fraud strategy

cards.title: OJK enforcement in numbers (to 30 October 2026)
cards.caption: Source: OJK press release SP 219/OJK/DKPU/XI/2026 (5 November 2026). Suspects are presumed innocent until a court decides.

items.label: Cases completed by OJK investigators
items.detail: Total investigations completed across all sectors up to 30 October 2026.

items.label: Of them in banking
items.detail: The largest share of completed investigations.

items.label: Cases decided by courts
items.detail: Of which 163 are final and binding.

items.label: Rural bank directors
items.detail: Handed with evidence to prosecutors in Batu on 30 October 2026, as suspects.

cards.title: Real case: bank directors before prosecutors (2026)
cards.body:
OJK's press release of **5 November 2026** reported that OJK investigators had handed **two suspects and the evidence** to the public prosecutor at the Batu district prosecutor's office on **30 October 2026**. The suspects were the president director and a director of a conventional rural bank (BPR), identified only by initials.

- Earlier, OJK investigators had submitted the case file and been told on 14 October 2026 that it was complete.
- OJK has its own investigators for financial sector crimes. By 30 October 2026 they had completed 191 cases, 152 of them in banking.
- The individuals are suspects; only a court can decide guilt.

**Lesson:** when fraud reaches the top of a bank, the consequences go beyond administrative sanctions. Early internal reporting, through a channel staff trust, is often the best chance to stop it.

cards.title: Getting ready for OJK's review
cards.caption: A readiness checklist built from POJK 17/2023, POJK 24/2022, SEOJK 28/2022 and POJK 12/2024.

items.label: Governance
items.left: Report filed and published within 4 months; self-assessment twice a year
items.right: Late filing; inflated ratings; no action plan

items.label: Boards and committees
items.left: Composition, charters reviewed every 3 years, minutes with dissent
items.right: Directors on commissioners' committees; vacant expert seats

items.label: Certification
items.left: Register of certificates, expiry dates and recognised refreshers
items.right: Lapsed certificates with no replacement plan

items.label: Staff development
items.left: At least 3.5% of prior-year gross salary spent; plan in business plan
items.right: Budget met on paper but not spent

items.label: Anti-fraud and whistleblowing
items.left: Yearly anti-fraud education; trusted, confidential channel; cases tracked
items.right: No protection from retaliation; reports go to the person reported

cards.question: How often must Bank Rinjani Raya educate its own staff on its anti-fraud policy under POJK 12/2024?
options: Only when a new employee joins
Once every three years
Only after a fraud has occurred
At least once a year
cards.explanation: Article 7 requires institutions to provide education and competence development to internal parties, and education or socialisation to external parties, on the anti-fraud policy at least once a year.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: POJK 12/2024 requires a four-pillar anti-fraud strategy; whistleblowing is part of the detection pillar.
Reporters' identities stay confidential, anonymous reports are possible, retaliation is banned, and true reports can be rewarded.
The anti-fraud unit answers to a director with a direct line to the commissioners; investigators must be independent and competent.
Anti-fraud education for staff, and outreach to outsiders, happen at least once a year.
OJK readiness means evidence: governance reports, committee records, certificate registers, development spending and tracked fraud cases.

cards.prompt: If you saw something wrong at work tomorrow, would you know which channel to use and what protection you have? What would make you trust that channel more?

quiz.question: Which pillar of the POJK 12/2024 anti-fraud strategy contains the whistleblowing policy and mechanism?
options: Prevention
Monitoring, evaluation and follow-up
Investigation, reporting and sanctions
Detection
quiz.explanation: The attachment to POJK 12/2024 places the whistleblowing policy and mechanism in the detection pillar, together with surprise audits and surveillance systems.

quiz.question: A customer wants to report a bank employee's fraud without giving her name. What does POJK 12/2024's guidance say?
options: Anonymous reports are possible, and outsiders may report too
Reports must be signed so that the bank can verify the reporter
Only employees may use the whistleblowing channel, not customers
She must file her report directly with the police
quiz.explanation: The guidance aims the policy at both employees and external parties and states that reporting can be anonymous.

quiz.question: Two weeks after reporting suspected bribery, a staff member is suddenly given poor ratings by the manager she reported. What principle is at stake?
options: The ban on retaliation against whistleblowers
The bank's right to manage staff performance freely and quickly
The duty to report fraud to OJK within a day
The rule on concurrent positions for staff
quiz.explanation: POJK 12/2024's guidance requires full support and protection for reporters, including a ban on retaliation and confidentiality of identity. An adverse act by the person reported calls for review.

quiz.question: To whom must the anti-fraud unit or function answer under POJK 12/2024?
options: The head of internal audit, with no line to either board
The controlling shareholder, through its own audit team
A director, with a direct line to the commissioners
The branch network head, with a monthly report to OJK
quiz.explanation: Article 8 requires the unit or function to be responsible to a member of the Board of Directors and to have a direct communication and reporting line to the Board of Commissioners.

quiz.question: What does POJK 12/2024 expect the head of the anti-fraud unit to have?
options: A law degree and a background in the national police
Anti-fraud certification, anti-fraud experience and/or sector experience
At least ten years as a director of the same bank
A risk management certificate at the top level of the national qualifications framework
quiz.explanation: Article 8(3) requires the head of the unit or the officer in charge to have an anti-fraud expertise certificate, anti-fraud experience and/or adequate experience in the relevant financial sector.

quiz.question: Which of these is NOT a fraud type listed in Article 2 of POJK 12/2024?
options: Overstating net income in financial statements
Leaking confidential information
Misusing the bank's cash
Making a loan that later defaults for genuine business reasons
quiz.explanation: Article 2 lists corruption, asset misappropriation, financial statement fraud, deception, leaking confidential information and similar acts. A genuine credit loss is not fraud.

quiz.question: Fajar's report names his branch manager. The regional audit team that would normally investigate reports to the same regional head. What should the bank do?
options: Let the regional team proceed as usual, to save time and cost
Assign investigators whose independence and competence fit the case
Ask the branch manager to explain the whole matter in writing first
Close the case unless Fajar provides documents
quiz.explanation: The investigation standard in POJK 12/2024 requires the bank to decide who may investigate with regard to the independence and competence needed, and to keep information confidential.

quiz.question: Which channel list matches the examples POJK 12/2024's guidance gives for receiving fraud reports?
options: Only a locked box at head office
Only a telephone hotline run by OJK
Website, messaging apps, phone, letter, email and fax
Only face-to-face meetings with the compliance director
quiz.explanation: The guidance lists several ways to receive reports, including website, electronic messaging apps, telephone, letter, email, fax and other means.

quiz.question: A director ignores repeated written warnings for failing to make the anti-fraud strategy effective. What further sanction can OJK impose on the director personally under POJK 12/2024?
options: A personal administrative fine of Rp50 billion for each breach
A ban on acting as a main party of a financial institution
Freezing of all the director's personal bank accounts
An automatic criminal conviction
quiz.explanation: Article 9(4) allows OJK, after a written warning, to bar directors and/or commissioners who keep breaching certain duties from being main parties, under OJK's reassessment rules.

quiz.question: According to OJK's November 2026 press release, what had happened to the two rural bank directors in the Batu case?
options: OJK investigators handed them and the evidence to prosecutors as suspects
A court convicted them and banned them for life
OJK fined them and closed the case
They were cleared after the case file was rejected
quiz.explanation: OJK reported that on 30 October 2026 its investigators handed two suspects, the president director and a director of a rural bank, with evidence to the Batu district prosecutor, after the case file was declared complete. They remain suspects until a court decides.

references.note: Real case: OJK says it will intervene to secure governance, risk and compliance and urges banks to watch cyber, economic crime and climate risks.

bank.question: A new board member asks where POJK 17/2023 expects good governance to apply. Which answer is accurate?
options: Only in decisions taken by the Board of Directors
Only in activities that OJK has examined in the last two years
Only at head office, not in branches or subsidiaries
In all its activities, at every level of the organisation
bank.explanation: Article 2 requires banks to apply good governance in their business activities and other activities at all levels of the organisation, in line with the law.

bank.question: Bank Rinjani Raya has no written internal procedure on applying good governance, only board charters. What does POJK 17/2023 require?
options: An internal governance procedure, evaluated and updated to stay compliant
Nothing more, because board charters are enough
A procedure approved in advance by OJK
A procedure only if the bank is listed
bank.explanation: Article 3 requires banks to have internal procedures on applying good governance and to evaluate and update them so they meet the law. Breach can lead to a written reprimand and further sanctions.

bank.question: The audit committee asks how OJK uses the bank's governance self-assessment. Which description is correct?
options: OJK files it without any review unless the overall rating is poor or worse
OJK evaluates it and may demand an action plan or a special examination
OJK uses it only to set the bank's deposit insurance premium
OJK forwards it to the controlling shareholder for approval
bank.explanation: Article 133 says OJK assesses or evaluates the bank's self-assessment, can ask for an action plan with corrective steps and target dates, may ask for changes to the plan and may carry out a special examination.

bank.question: Bank Rinjani Raya publishes its governance report on its website five weeks after the four-month deadline. How is the bank classed?
options: As late, because any delay counts only as late
As compliant, because the report was eventually published
As late only if OJK has sent a reminder letter
As not having published the report, because it is more than one month late
bank.explanation: Article 131 treats submission or publication within one month after the deadline as late; beyond that one month, the bank is treated as not having submitted or published the report.

bank.question: A bank keeps breaching POJK 17/2023 after a written reprimand. Which statement about possible sanctions is accurate?
options: OJK can only repeat the written reprimand each year until it is fixed
OJK must refer every governance breach to the police first
OJK can restrict activities, and main parties can be barred
Only the controlling shareholder can be sanctioned
bank.explanation: The sanction articles allow, after a written reprimand, bans on new products, freezing of activities, bans on expansion or new activities and a lower governance rating; main parties may be barred under OJK's reassessment rules, and fines can apply to the bank and/or controlling shareholder.

bank.question: A controlling shareholder is found to have pushed the bank into a governance breach. Under POJK 17/2023, can a fine be imposed on the shareholder itself?
options: No, only the bank as a legal entity can be fined under POJK 17/2023
Yes, but only up to Rp500 million per year, however many breaches there are
No, shareholders can only be warned in writing
Yes: Rp2 billion to Rp50 billion per violation, on the bank and/or shareholder
bank.explanation: The sanction articles of POJK 17/2023 allow an administrative fine on the bank and/or the controlling shareholder of at least Rp2 billion and at most Rp50 billion for each violation.

bank.question: Which pair are both among the sixteen aspects listed in Article 2(4) of POJK 17/2023?
options: Remuneration, and brand marketing strategy
Remuneration, and integrity of reporting and IT systems
Branch expansion, and integrity of reporting
Dividend policy, and sustainable finance
bank.explanation: The sixteen aspects include remuneration, integrity of reporting and IT systems, the strategic plan, shareholder aspects, anti-fraud and anti-bribery, sustainable finance and group governance. Marketing, branch expansion and dividend policy are not among them.

bank.question: According to OJK's FAQ on SEOJK 14/SEOJK.03/2025, from which reporting position did banks first submit a self-assessment covering all sixteen factors?
options: The December 2025 position
The June 2024 position
The December 2023 position
The June 2027 position
bank.explanation: The FAQ states that banks submit a self-assessment covering the 16 factors for the first time for the December 2025 position, with deadlines following the soundness rating rules. SEOJK 14/2025 took effect on 24 June 2025.

bank.question: Which statement about OJK's September 2023 announcement of POJK 17/2023 is accurate?
options: It was copied from Singapore's code of corporate governance for banks
It would apply only from 2026, after a three-year transition period
It drew on Basel Committee, OECD and IFC standards and the P2SK Law
It replaced the Banking Law
bank.explanation: OJK's press release of 19 September 2023 said the updated rules were aligned with international standards including those of the Basel Committee, the OECD and the IFC, and were a follow-up to Law 4/2023 (P2SK).

bank.question: Bank Rinjani Raya has four directors. Only one has five or more years of operational experience as a bank executive officer. What does POJK 17/2023 require?
options: A majority must have it, so at least three of the four
Only the president director needs that operational experience
At least one director with that experience is enough for any board
Half the directors, so two of the four, is enough
bank.explanation: Article 6(3) requires the majority of directors to have at least five years' operational experience as executive officers of a bank. With four directors, a majority means at least three.

bank.question: The board has three directors. One resigns in writing, which would leave two. When does the resignation take effect?
options: Immediately on receipt of the written notice
Only once the GMS has decided it and a new director has been appointed
Thirty days after the notice, whatever happens
Once OJK has approved the resignation letter
bank.explanation: Article 12(2) provides that a resignation that would leave fewer than three directors is valid only once the GMS has decided it and a new director has been appointed. OJK may evaluate whether a resignation was voluntary.

bank.question: A director holds 20 percent of a trading company and is offered shares that would take him to 26 percent as an ordinary purchase. What applies?
options: He may, if he discloses the stake in the governance report
He may not own 25 percent or more of another company's paid-up capital
He may, if the trading company is not a bank customer
He may, if the commissioners approve it in advance
bank.explanation: Article 16(1) bars directors, alone or jointly, from owning 25 percent or more of another company's paid-up capital. Only shares received as bonuses or tantiem are excepted.

bank.question: Which disclosure must every director and commissioner make in the governance report?
options: All personal bank balances and annual personal tax returns
Every share they own in any company anywhere, however small the stake
Holdings of 5% or more, and financial or family ties to key parties
Their votes on each credit decision during the year
bank.explanation: Articles 32 and 57 require disclosure of shareholdings of at least 5 percent in the bank or other companies, and of financial and second-degree family relationships with other board members and controlling shareholders.

bank.question: An independent commissioner has served two consecutive terms. The GMS wants to re-appoint her for a third. What must the decision consider?
options: Her performance, assessments of her independence and her own statement
Only the controlling shareholder's written approval of her track record
Only a new fit and proper test by OJK
Nothing: a third term is never allowed under any circumstances
bank.explanation: Article 40 allows re-appointment after two consecutive terms only after considering her performance, the commissioners' meeting view that she remains independent, a view from the head of internal audit and the HR executive, and her own statement on independence at the GMS.

bank.question: An independent commissioner is elected as a regional head of government. What does POJK 17/2023 say?
options: Independent commissioners may not hold a public office at the same time
She may keep both roles if she discloses it
She may keep both roles until her term ends
She must switch to non-independent commissioner
bank.explanation: Article 46(5) bars independent commissioners from holding concurrent positions as public officials.

bank.question: The directors want a well-known consultant to advise on day-to-day lending decisions, with authority to approve loans. What does POJK 17/2023 allow?
options: This is allowed if the consultant signs a confidentiality agreement
This is allowed if the commissioners approve the consultant's fee
Not this: advisers may not hold operational decision powers
This is allowed for up to one year at a time
bank.explanation: Article 26 bars directors from using individual advisers or professional services as experts or consultants, except for special projects, under clear contracts, by qualified independent parties who hold no structural post and have no authority over operational decisions.

bank.question: Which statement about commissioners' meetings under POJK 17/2023 is accurate?
options: All meetings may be held by email circulation instead of in person
Independent commissioners may always attend only by video link
Meetings are valid with any two commissioners present
Absent non-independent members may join by video in certain cases
bank.explanation: Article 55 requires all commissioners to attend in person at least twice a year, lets non-independent commissioners who cannot attend physically join face to face using IT, and requires a majority for quorum.

bank.question: A director's sister is married to the president commissioner. The board has three directors, none of whom are otherwise related. Is the board in breach of the family-ties rule?
options: Yes, any family tie at all between the two boards is banned outright
Yes, unless the GMS waives the rule
No: the ban is on a majority of directors, and only one is affected
No, because in-laws never count as family under the rule
bank.explanation: Article 17 bars a majority of directors from being related within the second degree to each other or to commissioners. One director out of three is not a majority. Check the facts carefully against the definitions in the bank's own policy.

bank.question: Which aspect of the Cirebon rural bank case did OJK say it examined before the bank went into resolution?
options: A full evaluation of management performance
A review of the bank's marketing campaigns only
A survey of customer satisfaction scores in every branch
A check of branch opening hours
bank.explanation: OJK said it stepped up supervision, imposed administrative sanctions and orders, evaluated management performance comprehensively and oversaw a recovery plan before placing the bank in resolution status.

bank.question: Which pair of experts must the independent parties on a conventional bank's risk monitoring committee include?
options: One with legal expertise and one with marketing expertise
One with risk management expertise and one with finance expertise
One with IT expertise and one with HR expertise
One with audit expertise and one with tax expertise
bank.explanation: Article 65(1) requires at least one independent commissioner, one independent party with risk management expertise and, for a conventional bank, one independent party with finance expertise.

bank.question: The remuneration and nomination committee has three members: an independent commissioner (chair), a non-independent commissioner and the director in charge of HR. What is wrong?
options: Directors may not be members; seat the HR executive or a staff representative
Nothing is wrong; the director in charge of HR is the natural choice for it
The chair must be the non-independent commissioner, not the independent one
The committee must also include an external lawyer
bank.explanation: Article 66 requires an independent commissioner, a non-independent commissioner and either the executive officer in charge of HR or an employee representative, and bars directors from membership.

bank.question: Before the committee meets, which attendance makes a remuneration and nomination committee meeting valid?
options: Any two members, whoever they are, provided that minutes are kept
All members without exception, including any external advisers
A majority, including an independent commissioner and the HR member
The chair alone, if minutes are kept
bank.explanation: Article 77(4) requires a majority of members, including one independent commissioner and one HR executive officer or employee representative, for the meeting to be held.

bank.question: Which body evaluates the performance of the directors' committees, and how often at minimum?
options: The audit committee, every quarter
The Board of Directors, at least at each financial year-end
OJK, every three years
The GMS, at each annual meeting
bank.explanation: Article 62(4) requires the directors to evaluate their committees' performance at least at the end of each financial year. Article 63(6) sets the same duty for the commissioners and their committees.

bank.question: Which task belongs to the remuneration and nomination committee under POJK 17/2023?
options: Recommending independent parties for the audit and risk monitoring committees
Approving large loans to related parties of the controlling shareholder group
Running the internal audit plan
Setting the bank's interest rates on deposits and loans
bank.explanation: Article 73 gives the committee duties on remuneration policy and nomination, including recommending candidates for the boards and the independent parties for the audit and risk monitoring committees, and assessing board performance.

bank.question: A candidate commissioner has a conflict of interest linked to his nomination. What does POJK 17/2023 expect?
options: He keeps it private until after the GMS has appointed him
The bank discloses it only in its next annual report to shareholders
Nothing, since commissioners do not make operational decisions
He discloses it in the fit and proper process; OJK may act on it
bank.explanation: Article 38(6) and (7) require candidates with conflicts or potential conflicts linked to their nomination to disclose them in the fit and proper assessment, and allow OJK to set necessary supervisory measures.

bank.question: Which statement about fit and proper requirements for bank directors is supported by POJK 17/2023 and SEOJK 28/2022?
options: Once approved by OJK, directors are never assessed again while they are in office
Fit and proper assessment applies only to commissioners, not directors
They need OJK approval and must keep integrity, competence and reputation
Approval depends only on holding a risk certificate
bank.explanation: Article 19 requires directors to meet OJK approval requirements and to keep integrity, competence and a good reputation while in office. SEOJK 28/2022 treats a risk management certificate as one aspect of competence, not the whole test.

bank.question: Which theme did OJK place first among the five strategic priorities of its 2026-2030 banking roadmap, announced in November 2026?
options: Cutting capital requirements for small banks
Merging all rural banks into commercial banks
Strengthening institutions and integrity
Removing foreign ownership limits
bank.explanation: OJK's press release SP 219/OJK/DKPU/XI/2026 listed five strategic priorities for the RP3I 2026-2030 roadmap, starting with strengthening institutions and integrity, followed by technology and digital resilience, market deepening, sustainable finance, and integrated licensing and adaptive supervision.

bank.question: A newly hired treasury dealer, an officer below executive level, joins Bank Rinjani Raya. What does SEOJK 28/2022 mean for her?
options: She needs a valid risk management certificate while in that post
She needs one only after three years in the job
She needs one only if she trades derivatives
She does not need one; treasury is not covered
bank.explanation: SEOJK 28/2022 covers officers below executive level in main operating units that take risk decisions, naming treasury, credit, IT and finance, and requires a valid certificate while they hold the post.

bank.question: Who issues the risk management certificate referred to in SEOJK 28/2022?
options: OJK's banking supervision department, directly and for each candidate
Bank Indonesia's training institute
A banking-sector certification body (LSP) registered with OJK
The bank's own HR division, after an internal exam
bank.explanation: The circular defines the certificate as proof of competence issued by a banking-sector LSP, licensed by the national professional certification agency (BNSP) and registered with OJK.

bank.question: A banking certification body offers to run a paid preparation course for its own candidates. What does SEOJK 28/2022 say?
options: This is encouraged by OJK as a way to raise the national pass rates
This is allowed if OJK approves the syllabus
Certification bodies may not offer training to their candidates
This is allowed only for fast-track candidates for the boards
bank.explanation: Section V point 5 bars banking LSPs from offering education or training to applicants or participants of risk management certification, including helping others prepare such services.

bank.question: Under the alignment rules in SEOJK 28/2022, to which qualification level is a serving director aligned once the process is complete?
options: Level 4 of the KKNI framework
Level 7 of the KKNI framework
Level 5 of the national qualifications framework
Level 10 of the KKNI framework
bank.explanation: Section IV point 5 explains that, after alignment, serving directors meet competence at KKNI qualification level 7, while serving commissioners meet level 6.

bank.question: A candidate commissioner wants to use the fast-track risk management test. What must accompany her application?
options: A letter from OJK confirming her fit and proper result in advance
Proof that she already holds a level 7 certificate from a recognised foreign body
A recommendation from the controlling shareholder only
A director's cover letter with the GMS decision or the committee's advice
bank.explanation: Section III requires a cover letter signed by a director (or by a commissioner if the directors cannot or will not sign), attaching the GMS decision appointing her, or the remuneration and nomination committee's recommendation if not yet appointed.

bank.question: Which statement about foreign competence certificates is correct under POJK 24/2022?
options: They are never accepted for staff of Indonesian commercial banks
They are accepted automatically, without any equivalence review
They can be recognised as equivalent through mutual recognition
They count only for staff working abroad
bank.explanation: Article 20 allows certificates issued abroad to be recognised as equivalent for the same competence field, if recognised by the home authority and/or issued by an internationally reputable body, with equivalence done by the banking LSP in coordination with the competent agency.

bank.question: Where must Bank Rinjani Raya set out its plan for developing staff quality under POJK 24/2022?
options: In a separate annual letter to the Ministry of Manpower
In its bank business plan, with realisation reported later
In the governance report only, as part of the self-assessment
In the annual financial statements' notes only
bank.explanation: Article 9 requires the plan in the bank business plan, covering programmes, participant numbers and ratios and the projected funding ratio, with realisation reported in the business plan realisation report and records kept.

bank.question: Two directors' certificates will lapse soon, and the bank has no system to track certificate expiry. Which POJK 24/2022 duty is most directly breached?
options: Keeping 3.5 percent of salaries in a separate reserve account
Monitoring that staff hold certificates and take refreshers
Appointing a director in charge of compliance
Publishing every staff certificate on the bank's website each year
bank.explanation: Articles 16 and 17 require an internal system or procedure to monitor development continuously and to monitor that staff hold certificates in OJK-set fields and follow periodic maintenance programmes.

bank.question: Bank Rinjani Raya's whistleblowing policy is a 40-page legal document only available on request from the legal division. Which expectation of POJK 12/2024 does it miss?
options: It must be approved by the police before it is used
It must be clear, easy to understand and openly communicated
It must be no longer than five pages, including annexes
It must be published in a national newspaper every year
bank.explanation: The detection pillar guidance requires a clear, understandable and workable whistleblowing policy, communicated transparently to the whole organisation and external parties and applied consistently to build trust.

bank.question: What does POJK 12/2024's guidance say about rewarding whistleblowers?
options: Reports proven true with adequate evidence can be rewarded
Rewards are banned because they encourage false or malicious reports
Rewards are paid by OJK, not by the institution
Every reporter is rewarded, regardless of the outcome of the case
bank.explanation: The guidance on whistleblower protection states that the institution has a mechanism to reward reporters whose reports are proven true and backed by adequate evidence.

bank.question: Which competences does POJK 12/2024 list as examples for fraud investigators?
options: Sales, marketing and customer service skills
Investigation, forensic accounting, computer forensics and interviews
Legal drafting and court litigation only, always handled by outside counsel
Credit scoring and loan pricing
bank.explanation: The investigation standard asks the institution to decide who investigates with attention to independence and the needed competence, such as analysis and investigation, forensic accounting, computer forensics, and fieldwork and interviews.

bank.question: A director argues that once a fraud case is closed internally, nothing more is needed. Which part of POJK 12/2024's strategy does this ignore?
options: Prevention, which ends once staff are hired
Detection, which applies only to external fraud
Investigation, which OJK carries out itself
Monitoring, evaluation and follow-up, including fixing the weak controls
bank.explanation: The fourth pillar requires monitoring of follow-up, evaluation of the fraud events and weak controls, and follow-up to improve the anti-fraud system.

bank.question: Which statement about know-your-employee measures under POJK 12/2024's prevention pillar is accurate?
options: They cover hiring, promotions, transfers and monitoring staff integrity
They apply only to new hires during their probation period
They replace the need for a whistleblowing channel at smaller banks only
They apply only to directors and commissioners
bank.explanation: The prevention pillar expects effective recruitment showing candidates' track records, risk-based selection reaching promotions, transfers and high-risk posts, and policies to know and monitor staff character, integrity, relationships, behaviour and lifestyle.

bank.question: A report about a director reaches the anti-fraud unit. The director asks the unit head to send the file to him 'for comment' before anything else. What should the unit head do?
options: Send the file, since the unit answers to a director anyway
Delete the report to avoid conflict at board level
Forward it to the controlling shareholder's audit team for review
Keep it confidential and use the line to the commissioners
bank.explanation: Article 8 gives the anti-fraud unit a direct communication and reporting line to the Board of Commissioners. Confidentiality of the investigation and of the reporter must be kept; the person reported should not control the file.

bank.question: An OJK examiner asks how the bank can show that its risk certification, development spending and whistleblowing duties are actually met. Which evidence is strongest?
options: A board resolution stating that the bank complies with all OJK rules in force
Training budgets that exceed the floor on paper
A policy manual signed by the president director and the commissioners
Certificate and refresher records, actual spending and a log of fraud reports
bank.explanation: OJK's rules ask for evidence of practice: banks must monitor and record certificates and refreshers (SEOJK 28/2022, POJK 24/2022), actually spend the development floor (POJK 24/2022), and track fraud reports through investigation and follow-up (POJK 12/2024).

bank.question: In the Batu case reported by OJK in November 2026, what stage had the case reached on 30 October 2026?
options: A court had issued a final conviction
OJK had closed the case for lack of evidence
The bank's licence had been revoked that day
Suspects and evidence were handed over to the public prosecutor
bank.explanation: OJK said its investigators handed the two suspects, a rural bank's president director and a director, together with evidence to the Batu district prosecutor on 30 October 2026, after the file had been declared complete on 14 October 2026.
